text:
devin: heads-up — noticed steady memory drift on dedicated-prod-01 during long-context runs (2k+ tokens). kv page count increases even when requests finish. suspected cross-request contamination but looks alignment-related.

kv-bot: automated alert: KV_PAGE_UTIL > 85% on node dedica-01 over 5m window.

devin: repro on staging with local load: start a single session with 4096 window, run several generation queries with intermittent model switching (fused <-> tiling kernels). memory climbs ~20MB per request.

sophia: I pulled a perf.trace from staging. quick note: when the runtime switches kernel type mid-session we see "kv_write" entries with offsets that differ by 8 bytes from prior writes. reads later use the old offset calculations and fetch wrong blocks -> stale tokens replayed.

sophia: snippet from trace (abbreviated):
```
[INFO] kmode change: fused_attention -> tiling_attention at seq=1536
[KV] write page_id=42 offset=0x1f40 len=4096 tag=0x7a
[KV] write page_id=43 offset=0x1f48 len=4096 tag=0x7a   <-- +0x8
[KV] read  page_id=42 offset=0x1f40 len=512 tag=0x7a
[KV] read  page_id=43 offset=0x1f40 len=512 tag=0x7a   <-- reads original offset
```

ryan: wow. that explains stale tokens we've been seeing in long-history chats. is the offset coming from kernel-specific alignment macro?

sophia: appears so. fused kernel pads KV entries for vector alignment, tiling kernel expects packed layout. the runtime's page-append path doesn't normalize offset metadata when kernels switch, so we append with mismatched alignment.

maria: do we have failing unit tests for kernel-switch sequences? I think we only test steady-state single-kernel flows.

devin: correct. I can repro with a small harness. plan: add a regression test that toggles kernels mid-context and validates KV read-after-write for entire lifetime. also add an assert in the page append that checks documented alignment invariants.

sophia: temporary mitigation: when routing policy forces kernel switch, add a flush+align step that rewrites pending KV pages to canonical alignment. that will be heavier but buys time.

maria: action items:
- devin: add test + assert + small fix to normalize offsets on append (ETA today)
- sophia: prototype flush+align mitigation and run canary (ETA tomorrow)
- ryan: update rolling deploy plan to keep older model variant until canary stable (ETA today)

devin: quick repro command I used:
```bash
./bin/repro --model xlarge-v1 --kernel fused --switch-to tiling --tokens 4096 --session-id repro-1767
```

devin: debug log to look for: `KV_ALIGN_MISMATCH` and `KMODE_CHANGE` entries. also grep for page ids that appear with two distinct offsets.

ryan: can you paste the small failing log where stale token sequence visible?

sophia: pasted below — you can see "echoed" tokens from prior request after kernel switch: 
```
[GEN] seq=1540 token="The" source=req-123
[GEN] seq=1541 token="quick" source=req-123
[GEN] seq=1542 token="brown" source=req-123
[GEN] seq=1543 token="fox" source=prev-789        <-- stale from previous session
```

maria: rough patch idea: canonicalize `KVEntry::write_offset()` to a minimal packed representation and store an explicit `alignment_tag` in the page header. reads must use tag-aware offset computation. if tag missing, fail fast.

devin: agree. failing fast is better than subtle contamination. I'll push a draft PR and tag @sophia @maria for review.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for staging cluster at 2026-03-19T02:15:00Z (rolling, 10% nodes).

ryan: thanks. once PR is up I'll schedule a quick test during the canary window.

sophia: small note: also check batching heuristics — batch fusion path sometimes merges requests across kernel-mode boundaries; ensure batch metadata preserves per-request kernel alignment. I think that's a secondary vector.

devin: noted. adding unit test for batch-fusion across kernel boundaries too.

maria: will follow up with a short postmortem draft once we confirm the root cause. adding labels: regression, kvcache, kernel-switch. :mag: :wrench:

devin: thanks all. I'll post the PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
